block-guide:
FABREMENT/CONTENT-SOURCE (Content Source) The slot of a Fabrement template: where the page's own content is drawn. Exactly one per template (it or core/post-content), at any depth. It belongs in save-template only; never put it in a page or a global block (save-content refuses it). A Fabrement template replaces the whole page: the theme's header and footer are not drawn. The frame places its own header and footer (core/block refs) and, if wanted, the title, date and image (core/post-title, core/post-date, core/post-featured-image) around the slot.
MARKUP (attributes only; no HTML of its own) <!-- wp:block {"ref":20} /--> <!-- wp:group {"tagName":"main","layout":{"type":"default"}} --> <main class="wp-block-group"><!-- wp:fabrement/content-source {"layout":{"type":"constrained"}} /--></main> <!-- /wp:group --> <!-- wp:block {"ref":21} /--> As an entry: {"name":"fabrement/content-source","attributes":{"layout":{"type":"constrained"}}}.
WIDTH The slot is drawn as core/post-content (<div class="entry-content wp-block-post-content ...">). It has no align setting. layout "constrained": text keeps the theme's content width and alignfull / alignwide sections inside the page still span the screen / wide width. layout "default": nothing is limited, plain paragraphs run edge to edge. Without a layout attribute the template's contentWidth decides ("full" = default, "constrained" = constrained). Do not put the slot in a group with layout "constrained": the slot then becomes a narrow column and full-width sections cannot leave it. Use a "default" group.
THEME FILES Never send templateId or rules as attributes: such a block is refused. The slot learns its template when drawn and reads the theme-file rules from that template's saved JSON; choose files with save-template contentSource. With no matching rule it shows the page content; on an archive or the blog index, that view's own content.
PITFALLS - A frame with two slots (or a slot plus core/post-content) is refused; none is refused too. - Only the slot is page content. Everything else in the frame is the same on every page using it.
CHECK Open a page assigned to the template: header, page content and footer each appear once, and a full-width section of the page reaches both screen edges.
